method: Q split by downstream terminal count; v = Q / (pi r^2) evaluated per segment and baked per path sample

cardiac_coupling.model: four-chamber time-varying elastance + three-element Windkessel (systemic, pulmonary) + compressed intramyocardial coronary branch
cardiac_coupling.ap_model: O'Hara-Rudy 2011 human ventricular myocyte (ORd), endo variant, 41 states, SciPy BDF
cardiac_coupling.pulse_envelope: aortic pressure of beat #2, rescaled to [0.72, 1.27] as a multiplicative modulation of arterial particle speed. The SHAPE is the heart model output; the rescaling range is a display choice and is declared.
cardiac_coupling.data_source: PhysioNet MIT-BIH Normal Sinus Rhythm Database (nsrdb) record 16265 (32 M, 22.24 h) — PUBLIC PLACEHOLDER, NOT THE USER'S OWN DATA

display_gain_note: applied to the three duct systems ONLY, and only to the on-screen particle speed. Every velocity reported in this file is the UNGAINED v = Q/A.

lingual_artery.flow_provenance: whole-tongue blood flow 0.3-0.6 mL/min/g on a ~70 g tongue; the value used is the midpoint of the implied 20-42 mL/min and is an ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE published estimate, not a measurement
lingual_artery.velocity_kind: MEAN cross-sectional velocity Q/A, time-averaged. The published Doppler bounds quoted below are PEAK SYSTOLIC velocities, which run roughly 3-5x the mean in a peripheral artery, so a mean velocity landing BELOW a peak-systolic range is the expected result, not a defect. Both numbers are reported unchanged.
lingual_artery.published_reference_source: lingual artery peak systolic velocity 20-70 cm/s (Doppler series)

facial_artery.flow_provenance: facial artery flow, adult; ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE published estimate
facial_artery.velocity_kind: MEAN cross-sectional velocity Q/A, time-averaged. facial_artery.published_reference_source: facial artery peak systolic velocity 25-80 cm/s (Doppler series)

venous_return.flow_provenance: venous return = the sum of the three arterial inflows built here; it is NOT an independent measurement

parotid_duct.published_reference_source: no published duct velocity exists. The bound quoted is what the published stimulated parotid flow (0.5-1.0 mL/min per gland) implies through a 1-3 mm duct; it is DERIVED, not measured.

reflux_audit.definition: a sample refluxes if its baked v <= 0, or if the path arclength fails to increase between two consecutive samples; both are counted
